blocks.p: Random play's own drop is −4.6 PR on the main 200 pairs: the Nackgammon positions were slightly easier for random play, so a drop mixes how a model copes with the new start with how hard the positions are; the test cannot separate the two.

One setting per model: a model asked at several settings shows the one with its highest stored risk judgement in league play, on an exact tie the first in league order (chosen from league results, never from this test); All settings shows every setup asked (2 more rows). Decision / Chat is the model type; after each name is its model class (the Class row filters every table and the chart) and under it the paired test's group, the setups from one original league, so a chat model can sit in the League 1 group. Every table further down shows every setup.

blocks.p: LFM2.5-24B-A2B on : 107 positions recorded without a valid choice (timeouts or missing choices), 38 in the main 200 pairs and 69 in the reserve; on its final 500 pairs 55 standard / 52 Nackgammon; Grok 4.7 high : 34 positions recorded without a valid choice (timeouts or missing choices), 15 in the main 200 pairs and 19 in the reserve; on its final 500 pairs 16 standard / 18 Nackgammon. They are not answers: each is scored by the primary rule (the position's Random error), with both sensitivity checks below. Every other asked setup gave a valid choice on every recorded position.
Method spec 2026-10-24 §10 (groups: §10.14)
Scope. These results hold for these rosters only; each group is the setups in the run from that original league.
The League 3 group currently has 3 setups (GPT-6 Astra medium , Claude Fable 5.1 high , Grok 4.7 high ); comparisons 2 and 3 rest on them.

Additions. Added under §10.14(g) after this test's results had been computed and read: d1-ultra and GLiDE (League 1 group); Claude Fable 5.1 high and Grok 4.7 high (League 3 group). They follow the Cup roster, not the results. The primary comparisons are shown both ways: with the additions (the primary result, §10.14(b)) and with the original members only (22 setups, §10.14(d)).

Nackgammon has the rules of backgammon; only the starting position differs. Each setup was asked 200 Nackgammon positions and 200 standard positions matched to them by phase, position class, number of legal plays and the gap between the two best plays. Error rate (PR) = 500 × mean GNUbg 2-ply equity loss. Drop = Nackgammon PR − standard PR on the same pairs; positive = worse on Nackgammon. A setup whose first-look 97.5% interval was wide and contained 0 was asked the 300 reserve pairs too (500 pairs). Every recorded position is scored: an invalid, timed-out or missing answer scores the position's Random error, with the sensitivity checks below. Label from the final 97.5% interval: kept (within ±5 PR), dropped (the data's “worse”), better or unclear. “Unclear” means the interval is too wide to decide; it is not evidence of equivalence.
A larger drop is consistent with relying on familiar positions but is not proof: Nackgammon positions also differ in structure. “Kept” is a valid result.

The paired test's standard-side prompt differs from the league prompt (no opening table; the starting setup on its own line), so the standard error rates here are not compared with league error rates.

Random's own drop: −4.56 PR on the main 200 pairs, −3.73 on all 500 (Random scores slightly better on the Nackgammon positions). It is shown next to every result. Random is computed exactly from GNUbg's 2-ply values (mean loss over all legal plays): it is never asked and is not extended by the stopping rule; it is reported on the main 200 pairs and on all 500.

No group (exploratory), in no group comparison: GPT-6.1 Terra (a setup that had played in no league before this test, §10.14(b)); Gemini 4 Argon low , added by Can's decision of 2026-10-28 instead of Gemini 4 Argon high , not because of the Cup roster (§10.14(h)).
Not a ranking: rows are in fixed order (group, then standard PR) and no table can be sorted.

OpenAI Google Anthropic xAI DeepSeek Liquid AI Alibaba Inception Fastino Perplexity Subquadratic Celeris EldanRing TypeSafe Zefan Cai Blockbrain Labs GNUbg weak, Random (programs) Above the dashed diagonal: higher error on Nackgammon.

blocks.p: Settings: GNUbg 1.08.003 rollout: 1,296 trials per play, cubeless, variance reduction on, quasi-random dice, no truncation, no late evaluation, chequer play 1-ply, seed 1, 8 threads, nice 19; candidates: top 5 at 2-ply plus every play any setup chose. The additions' chosen plays that had no rollout yet were rolled out later with the same settings, alone rather than alongside the other candidates of their positions; the earlier rollouts are unchanged.

No primary comparison changes direction between 2-ply and rollout values, either way. GNUbg's network learned standard play, so its values for early Nackgammon positions are likely less accurate; the check bounds that, it does not remove it.
Scope. These results hold for these rosters only; each group is the setups in the run from that original league.
